shorts.title: What you will learn: Recursion
shorts.hook: A function that calls itself needs a way to stop.
shorts.script: A function that calls itself needs a way to stop. Today a function calls itself. It sounds strange, but it solves many problems with little code. A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem. It needs a base case. The base case is the simplest problem, and it stops the calls. Each call has its own variables on the stack. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Recursion.

shorts.title: Recursion in one minute
shorts.hook: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem.
shorts.script: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem. It needs a base case. The base case is the simplest problem, and it stops the calls. Each call has its own variables on the stack. When the base case returns, the calls finish one by one. Think of Russian dolls. You open one, and a smaller one sits inside. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Recursion in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: The base case is zero. The sum of nothing is zero. Otherwise, the sum to n is n plus the sum to n minus one. Sum to four is four plus sum to three. That goes on down to zero. The answer is ten. The program prints ten. A recursive function calls itself. The base case stops the calls. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A wrong base case
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The program prints zero for factorial of five. The base case returns zero, and zero goes into every multiplication. The whole answer becomes zero. For a product, the base case must return one. The base case value goes into every multiplication. With zero, every product becomes zero. For factorial the base value must be one. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
